newsitem.title: UK: S&P rates Nationsbanc Fin Prods AAA counterparty.
newsitem.headline: S&P rates Nationsbanc Fin Prods AAA counterparty.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Thursday it assigned its AAA counterparty rating to NationsBanc Financial Products Inc (NFP).
NFP is a wholly-owned non-bank subsidiary of NationsBank N.A. and is incorporated in Delaware, S&P said.

"The AAA rating reflects NFP's bankruptcy remoteness, capitalisation, market risk coverage, and credit risk coverage based on Standard & Poor's stressed default probabilities and stringent operating guidelines," S&P said in a statement.

It said NFP is capitalised with $300 million in the form of common equity and subordinated debt to cover its operating costs and credit risk. "The company will also maintain a committed line of credit in the amount of $150 million, initially provided by NationsBank," it added.
S&P said NFP will intermediate derivative transactions with certain counterparties of NationsBank.

"To insulate against potential market risk associated with its third party counterparty portfolio, NFP will enter into exactly offsetting mirror transactions with NationsBank, on a fully collateralised basis," it said.

"NationsBank will post collateral in the form of high quality liquid securities, on a daily basis, to a third party trustee. NFP's capital and liquidity requirements will be tested weekly, using a Monte Carlo simulation credit model."
S&P said NFP has contracted with a financial institution active in the derivatives market to serve as its contingent manager.

"Certain events, including NFP's failure to maintain sufficient capital and insolvency events with respect to NationsBank will result in the termination of NFP's mirror transactions with its parent and wind down of its third party counterparty portfolio," it said.

"Following a wind down event, the contingent manager will be responsible for re-hedging and managing the market risk of NFP's portfolio to its final maturity according to the company's operating guidelines," S&P said.
The agency added that compliance with NFP's operating guidelines will be monitored by an independent auditor.
